title: A Postcards for the Interior
author: Kestrel Amberdale
blurb: Paloma Galloway, a translator losing a childhood language one borrowed word at a time, has perfected the smile that ends conversations. But when a song on the radio is one that was written and never recorded, they discover that staying invisible was never really an option. To get through this, they must return to the place where the story went wrong before the last bus to the old neighborhood is rerouted forever.
style: wry first-person narration with emotional depth
